records.name: Nova Scotia
records.summary: No province-specific trans law or hostile official pattern was found; federal criminal law and the federal human-rights framework apply uniformly. Halifax hosts a large, organised 2SLGBTQ+ community and institutional support (the national LGBT charity Egale Canada is based there), while the documented Canadian hostility pattern elsewhere concentrates in other provinces' school-board and library politics. Outside the capital, expect the rural small-town profile national surveys find worse for trans and non-binary people. Risk broadly at parity with the national picture.

records.name: Quebec
records.summary:
Quebec's recorded profile rests on the national data series: Statistics Canada's March 2026 release on police-reported hate crime (2024 data) shows gender-identity/expression-motivated incidents rising nationally for a fourth consecutive year — +8% to 139, nearly triple 2020 — and identifies no trans-specific provincial pattern for Quebec.

No Quebec-specific anti-trans legislation, ordinance or incident series appears in the surviving sources, alongside national NGO analysis of the same police data; the province's largest city anchors one of the country's most established organised 2SLGBTQ+ communities.

records.name: Ontario
records.summary:
No province-specific anti-trans statute, policy or official hostility is on record: while two other provinces have legislated restrictions on trans names, pronouns or care, Ontario's government has not.

Criminal law and human-rights protection operate federally and uniformly. The national police-reported hate-crime series (Statistics Canada, March 2026) shows gender-identity/expression-motivated incidents rising nationally — +8% to 139 in 2024, a fourth consecutive increase — without identifying a trans-specific provincial pattern for Ontario.
